concepts.def: A vision of something that isn't there
Giving human qualities to a non-human thing
The belief that life has no meaning
Repeating a word for emphasis or rhythm
Vivid language that creates a picture

walkthroughs.body_html:
'Is this a dagger which I see before me, the handle toward my hand?' — Macbeth, Act 2 Scene 1.

A hallucination in iambic pentameter. The dagger 'marshall'st me the way' — even Macbeth's tools personify his guilt.

'Out, damned spot! Out, I say!' — Lady Macbeth, Act 5 Scene 1.

The fierce woman of Act 1 is now sleepwalking, scrubbing imaginary blood. Repetition shows obsession; the prose form (no iambic pentameter) shows breakdown.

'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow, creeps in this petty pace from day to day' — Macbeth, Act 5 Scene 5.

On hearing his wife is dead, Macbeth declares life 'a tale told by an idiot. signifying nothing.' This is nihilism — the play's bleak final philosophy.
